newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati withdraws suit against army.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati withdraws suit against army.

text.p: An Indonesian judge said on Monday the country's ousted minority party leader had withdrawn a 50 billion rupiah ($21.74 million) lawsuit against a senior army officer over his remarks that she was planning a coup.

Judge Mohammed Tojib of the East Jakarta District Court said the defamation suit filed by Megawati Sukarnoputri against Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid, the chief of the socio-political division of the armed forces, had been withdrawn following an out-of-court settlement.
Lawyers for Hamid said he had retracted comments that Megawati was planning a coup, which were reported by the Surya daily on August 13.
They said the two sides had reached an out-of-court settlement but did not give details.

Megawati was not present in court but her lawyers confirmed the suit had been withdrawn. Megawati's chief lawyer R.O. Tambunan said no money was involved in the settlement and Hamid's retraction of his comments was sufficient.
Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, was ousted from the leadership of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) by a government-backed faction in June.
Her supporters held almost-daily protest meetings against her ouster until a government crackdown on July 27.
Police raided the PDI office to evict her supporters, setting which led to riots in Jakarta in which at least five people died.
Some 200 people have been taken into custody in the wake of the riots, which the government says were instigated by a left-wing group which had infiltrated Megawati's supporters.

Megawati has also challenged her ouster as the PDI chief and that lawsuit is continuing. She has also said she plans to sue the national election body for its refusal to accept her list of candidates for the 1997 general elections.
The body has accepted candidates from the faction which ousted Megawati in addition to lists from the other two recognised political parties -- the ruling Golkar and the United Development Party.
